user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages from my phone today. I’ve tried a few times, but they just won’t go through. Can you help me fix this?

Thank you for reaching out about your issue with sending picture messages (MMS). I can help you troubleshoot this problem.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD),
- Or your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps!

Thank you for providing your information, John. I’ve identified your account. To help you with sending picture messages (MMS), I’ll need to check a few things on your phone.

Could you please let me know:
- Are you able to make regular calls and send text messages?
- Are you currently connected to mobile data (not just Wi-Fi)?
- Are you seeing any error messages when you try to send a picture message?

Once I have this information, I’ll guide you through the next steps to resolve the issue.
Status Bar: 📶³ Good | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I can make regular calls and send text messages just fine. My phone shows that mobile data is on, and I see "5G" at the top. I don’t see any error messages when I try to send a picture message—they just don’t go through. What should I do next?

Thank you for the details. Since you have regular service, mobile data is on, and you see "5G," the basics for MMS should be working. The next step is to check if your phone’s MMS capability is functioning correctly.

Please use your phone’s diagnostic tool to check if it can send MMS messages. If you have a “can_send_mms” or similar diagnostic option, please run it and let me know the result. If you’re unsure how to do this, let me know your phone model, and I can guide you through the process.

Once we have this information, I’ll help you with the next troubleshooting steps.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I checked, and it looks like my phone says it cannot send MMS messages right now. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking. Since your phone reports it cannot send MMS messages, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN or missing MMSC URL is a common cause for MMS issues.

Please check your APN settings and let me know if you see an MMSC URL listed. If you’re not sure how to check this, I can guide you through the process. Would you like instructions on how to check your APN settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked my APN settings, and it looks like there isn’t an MMSC URL listed. What does that mean, and what should I do about it?

The absence of an MMSC URL in your APN settings means your phone doesn’t have the necessary information to send or receive picture messages (MMS). This is a common cause of the issue you’re experiencing.

To fix this, you should reset your APN settings to the default values provided by your carrier. After resetting, you’ll need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your phone?

I get a bit nervous with things like this—if I reset the APN settings and reboot my phone, will I lose any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Could you please reassure me before I do anything?

Resetting your APN settings and rebooting your phone will not delete any of your personal data, such as photos, messages, contacts, or apps. The APN settings only control how your phone connects to your carrier’s network for internet and MMS. Resetting them simply restores the correct network connection settings.

You can safely proceed with resetting your APN settings and rebooting your phone without worrying about losing any important information. If you’d like, I can guide you step-by-step through the process. Would you like to continue?
Okay, thank you for explaining that! Yes, please, I’d appreciate step-by-step help. I just want to make sure I do it right. What should I do first?

Of course! Here’s what you should do step-by-step:

1. Go to your phone’s Settings app.
2. Find and select “Network & Internet” or “Connections” (the exact name may vary by phone).
3. Tap on “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Networks.”
4. Select “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
5. Look for an option to “Reset to default” or “Reset settings.” Tap this option to reset your APN settings.
6. After resetting, restart (reboot) your phone to apply the changes.

Once your phone has restarted, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if you need help with any of these steps or if you run into any issues.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I followed your instructions and reset the APN settings, then restarted my phone. But I still can’t send picture messages—nothing has changed. Is there something else I should try?

Thank you for letting me know. Since resetting the APN settings and rebooting didn’t resolve the issue, let’s try a few more troubleshooting steps:

1. Please check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your device. Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS.
   - Go to your phone’s Settings.
   - Look for “Wi-Fi Calling” (it may be under “Connections” or “Network & Internet”).
   - If Wi-Fi Calling is ON, please turn it OFF.

After turning off Wi-Fi Calling, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if this helps or if you need guidance on how to find the Wi-Fi Calling setting.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. Should I go ahead and turn it off now? Will that affect my regular calls?

Yes, please go ahead and turn off Wi-Fi Calling. This will not affect your ability to make regular calls over the cellular network—your phone will simply use your carrier’s network for calls instead of Wi-Fi.

After turning off Wi-Fi Calling, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you need any further assistance.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated.

Thank you for your patience, and I understand how frustrating this can be. Let’s try a couple more steps to pinpoint the issue:

1. Please check your phone’s network mode preference:
   - Go to Settings > Network & Internet (or Connections) > Mobile Network.
   - Look for “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.”
   - Make sure it is set to “4G/5G preferred” or “LTE/5G.” If it’s set to “2G” or “3G,” change it to a higher mode.

2. Next, let’s check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions:
   - Go to Settings > Apps > Messaging (or your default messaging app).
   - Tap on “Permissions.”
   - Make sure “Storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled.

After making these changes, try sending a picture message again. Please let me know the results or if you need help with any of these steps.

App 'messaging' has permission for: storage, phone.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I checked, and my phone is already set to "4G/5G preferred" for the network mode. The messaging app also has permission for storage and phone. I tried sending a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. What else can we try?

Thank you for confirming those settings. Since you’ve already tried all the standard troubleshooting steps—resetting APN, rebooting, disabling Wi-Fi Calling, confirming network mode, and checking app permissions—and the issue persists, this may require more advanced technical support.
